chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Hilal ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man from the Magians who converted to Islam, and he had seven wives, and they converted with him: What should he do? He said, 'He keeps four and divorces three.'
And it is not permissible for a slave to contract marriage with more than two free women, nor with more than four female slaves.
ai.seo_question: How many wives can a convert to Islam keep if he already has more than four?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *al-jami'* (holding more than four wives) for a newly converted male, mandating the retention of four and the divorce of the rest, while also extending this limit to male slaves regarding free women and female slaves. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus on the immediate applicability of the Quranic limit upon conversion, distinguishing between the status of the husband and the specific constraints on slaves' marital capacity.
